# sysutils_service (Data Source)

Reads whether a service exists, starts at boot and is running, with the same init system backends as `sysutils_service`: `systemctl` when systemd booted the host, `rc-service`/`rc-update` when OpenRC did, as on Alpine Linux. Only status queries run, so nothing on the host changes and no root privileges are needed. Where neither systemd nor OpenRC runs, as in most containers or with SysV init, reading still succeeds: `init_system` says what runs instead and `supported` is false.

The data source uses the same init system detection and backends as the [`sysutils_service`](../resources/service.md) resource, so `enabled` and `running` mean what they mean there. A service that does not exist is not an error: `exists` is false, `enabled` and `running` are false, and the other attributes are null.

## What is run

| Init system | Commands |
|-------------|----------|
| `systemd` | `systemctl show --property=LoadState --property=Id`, `systemctl is-enabled` and `systemctl is-active` |
| `openrc` | `rc-service --exists`, `rc-update show <runlevel>` and `rc-service <name> status` |
| `sysvinit` or none | Nothing: `supported` is false and the service attributes are null |

None of these commands changes the host or needs root.

## Example Usage

### Read a service

```terraform
data "sysutils_service" "ssh" {
  # "ssh" on Debian and Ubuntu; systemd resolves the alias "sshd" to it.
  name = "sshd"
}

output "ssh" {
  value = {
    init_system = data.sysutils_service.ssh.init_system # "systemd", "openrc", "sysvinit" or null
    exists      = data.sysutils_service.ssh.exists
    unit        = data.sysutils_service.ssh.unit    # "ssh.service"
    enabled     = data.sysutils_service.ssh.enabled # starts at boot
    running     = data.sysutils_service.ssh.running
    active      = data.sysutils_service.ssh.active_state # "active", "failed", ...
  }
}
```

### Manage a service only where it exists

```terraform
data "sysutils_service" "firewalld" {
  name = "firewalld"
}

# Stop and disable firewalld where it is installed, so that it does not
# replace the rules of sysutils_firewall_rule. "== true" also handles hosts
# without a supported init system, where exists is null.
resource "sysutils_service" "firewalld" {
  count = data.sysutils_service.firewalld.exists == true ? 1 : 0

  name    = "firewalld"
  enabled = false
  state   = "stopped"
}
```

`exists`, `enabled` and `running` are null where `supported` is false, so compare them with `== true` in conditions: a null condition is an error in Terraform.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the service, as in `sysutils_service`. With systemd, a unit name such as `"nginx.service"`, `"nginx"` (short for `nginx.service`), `"getty@tty2.service"` or `"backup.timer"`; aliases are resolved to the unit they name. With OpenRC, the name of a script in `/etc/init.d`, such as `"nginx"`.

### Optional

- `runlevel` (String) OpenRC runlevel that `enabled` refers to. Defaults to `"default"`, the runlevel that `rc-update add` uses. Ignored with systemd.

### Read-Only

- `active_state` (String) The init system's own word for the run state: what `systemctl is-active` prints, such as `"active"`, `"inactive"`, `"activating"` or `"failed"`; with OpenRC the status `rc-service <name> status` reports, such as `"started"`, `"stopped"` or `"crashed"`. Null if the service does not exist. Null if `supported` is false.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the service starts at boot, as `enabled` of `sysutils_service` reports it: with systemd, only the `is-enabled` state `enabled` counts; with OpenRC, whether the service is in `runlevel`. False if the service does not exist. Null if `supported` is false.
- `enabled_state` (String) The init system's own word for the enablement: what `systemctl is-enabled` prints, such as `"enabled"`, `"disabled"`, `"static"`, `"indirect"`, `"enabled-runtime"` or `"masked"`; with OpenRC `"enabled"` or `"disabled"`. Null if the service does not exist. Null if `supported` is false.
- `exists` (Boolean) Whether the init system knows the service: with systemd, whether a unit of that name is loaded or has a unit file (a load state other than `not-found`); with OpenRC, whether `rc-service --exists` finds a script in `/etc/init.d`. Null if `supported` is false.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier (equal to `name`).
- `init_system` (String) Init system that booted the host, detected like `init_system` of the `sysutils_host` data source: `"systemd"` if `/run/systemd/system` exists, otherwise `"openrc"` if `/run/openrc/softlevel` exists, otherwise `"sysvinit"` if PID 1 is `init`. Null if none of them runs, as in most containers.
- `running` (Boolean) Whether the service is running, as `state` of `sysutils_service` reports it: with systemd, when `systemctl is-active` reports `active`, `reloading` or `refreshing`; with OpenRC, when `rc-service <name> status` reports `started`. False if the service does not exist. Null if `supported` is false.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether `init_system` is one that the data source and `sysutils_service` support: `"systemd"` or `"openrc"`. If false, the attributes describing the service are null.
- `unit` (String) Name the init system knows the service by: with systemd the unit's primary name, with its type suffix added and aliases resolved, such as `"ssh.service"` for `name = "sshd"`; with OpenRC `name` itself. Null if the service does not exist. Null if `supported` is false.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| systemd or OpenRC booted the host, but `systemctl`, or `rc-service` and `rc-update`, is not installed | `Init system tools not available` |
| `name` is not a valid name for the init system, such as `getty@tty1.service` with OpenRC | `Invalid service name` |
| A status command fails | `Querying service` |
| The provider's `root_dir` is set | `Not supported with root_dir` |

## Caveats

- SysV init is detected, and reported in `init_system`, but not supported: the data source runs no command there.
- With systemd, a unit that is loaded but has no unit file, such as one whose file was deleted while it runs, exists. A unit of which only an alias is given is reported under its primary name in `unit`.
- With OpenRC, `enabled` refers to one runlevel, `default` unless `runlevel` is set. A service in the `boot` runlevel only is not enabled in `default`.
- The data source reads the running host, so it refuses to work when the provider's `root_dir` is set.
- It is read during planning. A service that a `sysutils_package` or `sysutils_systemd_unit` resource in the same configuration creates is only seen if the data source depends on that resource.
